sections.label: Amending the WABA
sections.summary: The WABA has not been substantially amended since 1965, and it is now time to amend it and align it with other animal-related legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The WABA has not been substantially amended since 1965.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that it is now time to amend this Act and align it with other animal-related legislation that we have already strengthened.

sections.label: Chairing the committee
sections.summary: The speaker chairs a committee of passionate individuals whose first meeting was held in February 2018, more than two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am proud to chair this committee of passionate individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It feels like it was just yesterday, but we held our first meeting in February 2018, more than two years ago.

sections.label: First public consultation sessions
sections.summary: The first public consultation was a face-to-face session in May 2018, followed by an online REACH session from June to July 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The first public consultation was a face-to-face session in May 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It was then followed by an online session on REACH from June to July 2018.

sections.label: Online consultation responses
sections.summary: An online session on REACH from June to July 2018 followed, and over a thousand responses were received in the online consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It was then followed by an online session on REACH from June to July 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We received over a thousand responses in our online consultation.

sections.label: Proposed amendments and renaming
sections.summary: Sharing and listening produced proposed amendments strengthening protection, preservation and management of wildlife, and the Bill renames the Wild Animals and Birds Act as Wildlife Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Through sharing and, most importantly, listening, we have reached a set of proposed amendments that, I believe, strengthen the protection, preservation and management of wildlife for the purposes of maintaining a healthy eco-system and safeguarding our public safety and health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Bill will amend the Wild Animals and Birds Act by, first, renaming it Wildlife Act, from WABA to WA.

sections.label: Prohibiting release and feeding
sections.summary: New sections 5(a) and 5(b) prohibit releasing and feeding wildlife throughout Singapore unless approved by the Director-General, Wildlife Management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The new sections 5(a) and 5(b) in the Wildlife Act extend these by prohibiting the release and feeding of wildlife throughout Singapore, unless approved by the Director-General, Wildlife Management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: They do so out of compassion and a genuine desire to help animals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Thus, the solution cannot only be to rely on the law to regulate behaviour, but to first help them understand that the feeding and release of wildlife causes more harm than good, so they are internally motivated to change.

sections.label: NParks trap removal powers
sections.summary: New sections 10A, 11A and 11B empower NParks to dismantle unattended or unauthorised traps, with notice, or enter without notice if an offence is suspected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: One solution to this is the new section 10A, which empowers NParks to dismantle and dispose of unattended or unauthorised traps in any place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: If the place is owned or occupied, NParks will need to give reasonable notice in writing to the owner or occupier before conducting its checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: However, if an offence is suspected, such as if NParks receives a specific tip-off that poaching activities are being carried out on a private property, NParks will be empowered, under the new section 11A and 11B, to enter without notice to search for and seize the trap.

sections.label: Higher penalties for snare traps
sections.summary: The updated provision, now new section 7, includes snare traps so users face higher penalties like those for spring guns and pitfalls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The existing section 9 of WABA sets out higher penalties for wildlife traps that may also harm humans, such as spring guns or pitfalls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We have updated this provision, which is now in the new section 7, to include snare traps, so that those who use them will also be liable to higher penalties.

sections.label: Minister's exemption power
sections.summary: New section 20 empowers the Minister to exempt any person, place or wildlife, or classes of them, from provisions of the Act by Gazette order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The new section 20 empowers the Minister to exempt any person, place or wildlife, or any class of persons, places or wildlife, from any or all provisions of the Act by order in the Gazette.

sections.label: Protecting selected threatened species
sections.summary: Selected threatened species, including invertebrates, can be put on a list to be protected beyond parks and nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Selected threatened species, including invertebrates, can be put on this list, such that they can be protected beyond our parks and nature reserves.

sections.label: Higher penalties for wildlife offences
sections.summary: Clauses 7, 9, 10 and 12 introduce higher penalties for all offences to align the Wildlife Act with the ABA, ESA and PTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Illegally trading in exotic pets is only punishable by a fine of up to $1,000 under the existing Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Clauses 7, 9, 10 and 12 thus introduce higher penalties for all offences to bring the Wildlife Act on par with more updated animal-related legislation, namely the ABA, ESA and PTA.

sections.label: Poaching versus illegal import penalties
sections.summary: Poaching and local selling carries a fine up to $1,000 under the existing Act, while illegally importing a poached pangolin can be penalised up to $50,000 and/or two years' imprisonment under the ESA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Poaching and selling it locally would only be liable to a fine of up to $1,000 under the existing Act, whereas illegally importing a pangolin which was poached elsewhere could be penalised by up to $50,000 and/or two years' imprisonment under the ESA.

sections.label: Penalties for protected species offences
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 9 make killing, trapping, taking, keeping, selling or exporting protected species punishable by up to $50,000 in fines and/or two years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 9 set out that killing, trapping, taking, keeping, selling or exporting these protected species will be punishable by the highest penalties under the Act – up to $50,000 in fines and/or two years' imprisonment, on par now with the ESA.

sections.label: Wildlife EIA directions offences
sections.summary: Wildlife-related EIA conditions can be issued as directions, and contravention is an offence punishable by up to $50,000 in fines and/or six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The relevant wildlife-related EIA conditions can thus be formally issued as directions, and contravention of these directions would constitute an offence punishable by up to $50,000 in fines and/or six months' imprisonment.

sections.label: Limits on forfeiture of conveyances
sections.summary: The Court may not order forfeiture of very large conveyances, aircraft or trains used for regular passenger service, or conveyances used unlawfully without the owner's knowledge or consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Court may not order the forfeiture of very large conveyances or aircrafts or trains used for regular passenger service to and from Singapore, as well as conveyances that were used unlawfully without the owner's knowledge or consent.

sections.label: Clarifications on sections 5A and 5C
sections.summary: The Member has two clarifications on new sections 5A and 5C, and finds the word "intentional" in section 5A may be challenging to enforce as it puts the burden on the state to prove intent.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, I have two clarifications relating to the new sections 5A and 5C which set out the offences of feeding, releasing, killing, trapping, taking or keeping of wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In relation to the new section 5A which makes intentional feeding of any wildlife without approval an offence, I find that the use of the word “intentional” may be a challenging one to enforce, as it puts the burden on the state to prove intent.

sections.label: Offence under new section 5C
sections.summary: The new section 5C makes it an offence to intentionally kill, trap, take or keep wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The new section 5C makes it an offence to intentionally kill, trap, take or keep wildlife.

sections.label: Importing living wildlife without approval
sections.summary: The second clarification relates to the offence of importing living wildlife without approval under the new section 9(1).

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: My second clarification relates to the offence of importing living wildlife without approval under the new section 9(1).

sections.label: Retaining deterrent and CITES trade regulation
sections.summary: The speaker believes a deterrent should be retained and the CITES Convention adopted to regulate trade in live animals, animal parts and animal-based products.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is my strong belief that we should retain that as a deterrent to anyone who might want to reignite such practices.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We should adopt the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora and regulate not just the trade of live animals but also that of animal parts and animal-based products in order to ensure that wildlife species are not threatened to extinction by trade.

sections.label: Clause 4 covers invertebrates
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends the definition of "animal" to include invertebrates as well as vertebrates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One of the ways it does this is by regulating, not just vertebrates, but also invertebrates, through clause 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That clause amends the definition of “animal” to include, among many others, invertebrates.

sections.label: Section 5 excludes trapping
sections.summary: Under section 5, the Act currently includes taking, killing and keeping, but not trapping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Currently, under section 5, the Act includes taking, killing and keeping, but not trapping.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for subsequent offenders
sections.summary: Penalties are enhanced across the board and also enhanced for subsequent offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Not only are there enhanced penalties across the board, there are also enhanced penalties for subsequent offenders.

sections.label: Tenfold fine and custodial sentence
sections.summary: The Bill increases the fine 10-fold to $10,000 and adds a possible custodial sentence of up to six months, with a clarification sought on authorised officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill increases this 10-fold to $10,000 and even adds on a possible custodial sentence of up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If I may, Sir, I wish to seek clarification that the authorised officer in the new section 12K in clause 13 is intended to refer to an authorised officer who is authorised by the Director-General to compound offences and is not referring to authorised officers generally.

sections.label: Pigeon feeding penalties compared
sections.summary: Feeding stray pigeons is an offence under the Animals and Birds (Pigeons) Rules with a fine not exceeding $500, while the Bill may make it an offence with fines of $5,000 or $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under Rules 10 and 17 of the Animals and Birds (Pigeons) Rules enacted under the Animals and Birds Act, it is an offence to feed stray pigeons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The punishment upon conviction is a fine not exceeding $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The proposed section 3(1)(a) in this Bill preserves the operation of the Animals and Birds Act. "Pigeons", it appears, may satisfy the definition of "wildlife", too, under this amendment Bill, in which case, the feeding of pigeons will be an offence under the proposed section 5A in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The punishment is a fine not exceeding $5,000 for a first offender and $10,000 for a subsequent offender.

sections.label: Community sentencing and fine-only offences
sections.summary: Community-based sentencing orders like Mandatory Treatment Orders cannot be made for fine-only offences under the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Criminal Procedure Code, community-based sentencing orders, such as Mandatory Treatment Orders (MTOs), may not be made in respect of fine-only offences.

sections.label: Bill relevance to COVID-19
sections.summary: The Bill is highly relevant to the COVID-19 crisis because novel coronaviruses are endemic to many wildlife populations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill is actually highly relevant to the current COVID-19 crisis because novel coronaviruses are known to be endemic to many wildlife populations.

sections.label: Maximum fine for first offence
sections.summary: The maximum fine for the first offence is $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The maximum fine is $5,000 for the first offence.

sections.label: Risk to vehicle-for-hire operators
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned this puts operators of vehicles for hire at risk of having their livelihood seized.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What I am concerned about is that this puts operators of vehicles for hire at risk of having their livelihood seized.

sections.label: Section 10 directions and proportionality
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether section 10 lets private parties sue the Government over development works and why there is no proportionality clause.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Government development projects, such as the Cross-Island Line, could significantly affect the eco-system and wildlife if measures are not taken.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does Mr Ng think that section 10 grants private parties the right to sue the Government to issue directions on development works, whether carried out by other private parties or by the Government itself?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, I am concerned there is no proportionality in section 10.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is no requirement in the Bill that the Director-General consider the actual costs of remediation, the likely benefits to the eco-system and wildlife, and the relative social and ecological value of the wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should we actually put in the same effort to protect common pigeons as we do pangolins?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I wish to ask Mr Ng why there is no proportionality clause and on what principles he thinks the Director-General should proceed in issuing directions under the Act.

sections.label: Preference for Select Committee
sections.summary: The speaker's concerns are substantive, particularly on section 10 directions and sections 11B and 12C seizure and forfeiture powers, and prefers sending the Bill to a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The concerns I have raised are in some areas quite substantive, particularly on the section 10 powers of the Director-General to issue directions on development works, and on sections 11B and 12C powers of seizure and forfeiture of conveyances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My preference is that we should send the Bill to a Select Committee rather than pass it immediately.

sections.label: Caged bird trade regulation
sections.summary: The speaker asked MND to consider the IUCN Red List for the caged bird trade and welcomes amendments raising fines and closing loopholes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I have asked MND to consider adopting the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List to regulate the caged bird trade as well as touched on stiffening the penalties in the illegal wildlife trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad that the proposed amendments include enhancing the fines for offenders as well as closing some technical loopholes.

sections.label: Bird smuggling and traceability
sections.summary: Tar glue traps other birds, and unlike dogs, pet birds lack micro-chipping, encouraging illegal import and smuggling that cannot be detected in shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the destructive techniques they engage involves applying tar glue on tree branches, which ends up trapping other birds or female specimens of target species.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, while MND has introduced micro-chipping for dogs to improve traceability and in order to prevent illegal puppy mills, so far, these measures have not been introduced for birds sold as pets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The lack of measures encourages the illegal import and smuggling of birds as the culprit knows that once placed into a bird shop, it is impossible to differentiate a bird imported legally versus another imported illegally.

sections.label: Fine amounts for offences
sections.summary: A first offence carries a fine not exceeding $5,000, and a second or subsequent offence not exceeding $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If it is a first offence, the fine will not exceed $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As for a second or subsequent offence, the fine will not exceed $10,000.

sections.label: City in Nature budget
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee announced in the Budget that Singapore will become a City in Nature with 200 more hectares of nature parks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent Budget announcement by Minister Desmond Lee that Singapore will evolve from a City in a Garden to a City in Nature with another 200 hectares of nature parks added to act as complementary habitats and to buffer nature reserves from urbanisation is to be rejoiced.

sections.label: Definition of wildlife
sections.summary: The Member is asked to confirm whether the definition of wildlife extends to all wild marine animals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Member confirm that the definition of "wildlife" does, indeed, extend to all wild marine animals?

sections.label: Sections 8 and 9 trading
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify if sections 8 and 9 will apply to commercial aquariums trading wild marine animals when enacted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if sections 8 and 9 will be imposed on the trading of wild marine animals by commercial aquariums when enacted?

sections.label: Sharks and ray trade transparency
sections.summary: Asked whether the Ministry will work with other Ministries on transparent, traceable shark and ray trade reporting and recommend an HS code review to MEWR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the spirit of our progressive stance on wildlife protection, will the Ministry align with relevant Ministries to ensure collection and reporting of accurate sharks and ray trade information by Singapore as a key importer/exporter be made transparent and traceable, and will the Ministry recommend a review of the existing HS codes to MEWR?

sections.label: Cross Island Line and nature reserves
sections.summary: Asked whether section 10(1) can safeguard the Central Catchment Nature Reserve and other nature reserves if the Parks and Trees Act interpretation is contested.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given that the building of the Cross Island Line runs 70 m deep under the Central Catchment Nature Reserve (CCNR), would section 10(1) be able to safeguard the CCNR and other nature reserves should the interpretation of the Parks and Trees Act come into contention?

sections.label: City in Nature transformation
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said during Committee of Supply debates that natural capital will be enhanced and extended to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As Minister Desmond Lee shared during the Committee of Supply debates earlier this month, we will enhance and extend our natural capital across the island to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

sections.label: Wild Animals and Birds Act Bill
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng's Private Members' Bill to amend the Wild Animals and Birds Act complements MND's greening and biodiversity conservation plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng's Private Members' Bill to amend the Wild Animals and Birds Act complements MND's plans for the next bound of greening Singapore and conserving our biodiversity.

sections.label: Monitoring wildlife feeding hotspots
sections.summary: NParks will monitor feeding hotspots and take strong action against recalcitrant feeders unresponsive to engagement, advisories and warnings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: NParks will monitor feeding hotspots and take strong action against recalcitrant feeders who remain unresponsive to engagement, advisories as well as warnings.

sections.label: Repealing Pigeons Rules feeding rules
sections.summary: MND will repeal the feeding and release rules of the Animals and Birds (Pigeons) Rules, with wildlife feeding regulated under the Wildlife Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MND will be repealing the feeding and release rules of the Animals and Birds (Pigeons) Rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The feeding of wildlife, including wild birds, will be regulated under the Wildlife Act.

sections.label: Director-General wildlife feeding approval
sections.summary: The Director-General may approve feeding wildlife for research and professional wildlife rehabilitation based on his assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For instance, based on his assessment, the Director-General may grant approval to feed wildlife in situations, such as research and professional wildlife rehabilitation.

sections.label: Pet shop bird accounting
sections.summary: Licensing conditions require pet shops to ensure each bird in the shop is accounted for.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As part of these licensing conditions, pet shops are required to ensure that each bird in the shop is accounted for.

sections.label: CITES shark and ray product codes
sections.summary: Product codes have been created for all 41 CITES-listed shark and ray species permitted for commercial trade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Product codes for all the 41 species of CITES-listed sharks and rays that are permitted for commercial trade have been created.

sections.label: Act does not bind Government
sections.summary: The Act does not bind the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, the Act does not bind the Government.

sections.label: No private right to sue
sections.summary: The Act does not give private parties the right to sue the Director-General to issue directions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The power may be exercised by the Director-General “from time to time” and “as the occasion requires”, as is stated in the explanatory statement of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Thus, the Act does not confer private parties the right to sue the Director-General to issue directions to any party.

sections.label: Enforcing developer mitigation measures
sections.summary: The Bill lets NParks issue formal directions with penalties for developers failing certain wildlife-related mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Developers are required to implement the EMMP, the specifics of which, including the costs and benefits of the measures, are discussed between the developers and the technical agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This Bill closes a gap in the enforceability of some of these mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, NParks is unable to enforce against developers that fail to comply with certain wildlife-related mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Under the amended Act, NParks would be able to issue these requirements as formal directions and there would be penalties for non-compliance.

sections.label: Penalties for wildlife non-compliance
sections.summary: Non-compliance with wildlife-related measures is an offence, and section 10 provides penalties such as a fine or imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Non-compliance with such wildlife-related measures is an offence and section 10 provides for penalties, such as a fine or imprisonment.

sections.label: Compoundable wildlife offences prescribed
sections.summary: MND will prescribe compoundable offences in subsidiary legislation to the Wildlife Act and intends to allow composition of feeding and release offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Compoundable offences will be prescribed by MND in the subsidiary legislation to the Wildlife Act, and MND intends to allow for the composition of offences related to feeding and release.

sections.label: Repeal of Wild Animals Licensing Order
sections.summary: The WALRC recommended repealing the Wild Animals (Licensing) Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: First, the WALRC recommended repealing the Wild Animals (Licensing) Order.

sections.label: MND agrees to repeal Licensing Order
sections.summary: As the Licensing Order is subsidiary legislation, no Act-level amendment is required, and MND has agreed to repeal it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As the Licensing Order is a subsidiary legislation, no Act-level amendment is required, but I am glad to share that MND has agreed to repeal it.

sections.label: Wildlife management companies regulation consultation
sections.summary: The WALRC consulted the Singapore Pest Management Association, which supported upskilling workers, and regulating wildlife management companies needs no Act-level amendments under the existing ABA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The WALRC also consulted the Singapore Pest Management Association and its members, who were supportive of this opportunity to upskill their workers and improve the professionalism of the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: However, the proposal to regulate wildlife management companies would not require Act-level amendments, as it can already be done under the existing ABA.

sections.label: Starlings removed from Schedule
sections.summary: After discussions with MND and NParks, the purple-backed starling and Philippine glossy starling will be removed from the Schedule as they are no longer common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: After discussions with MND and NParks, I understand that the purple-backed starling and the Philippine glossy starling will be removed from the Schedule, as these species are no longer common.

sections.label: Pests and invertebrates not criminalised
sections.summary: The intent is not to criminalise killing and trapping of pests and non-threatened invertebrates, as these do not undermine wildlife protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my opening speech, the intent is not to criminalise the killing and trapping of pests and non-threatened invertebrates, as such activities do not undermine the overall aim of wildlife protection.

sections.label: NParks considers intent before prosecuting
sections.summary: Sun Xueling shared that NParks will consider intent and impact, including preventing further harm, before deciding to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling has shared that NParks will consider the intent and impact of someone's actions, including whether they were trying to prevent further harm, before deciding to prosecute.

sections.label: Consolidating wildlife feeding legislation
sections.summary: The intent is to consolidate legislation against feeding wildlife, including wild birds, under the Wildlife Act with higher penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Mr Murali is right that the intent is to consolidate the legislation against feeding of wildlife, including wild birds, under the Wildlife Act with higher penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling has shared that MND intends to repeal the relevant rules in the Animals and Birds (Pigeons) Rules in due course.

sections.label: Parks feeding fines up to $5,000
sections.summary: Under existing Parks and Trees Regulations, feeding and release of wildlife in parks are punishable with a fine of up to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: For example, under the existing Parks and Trees Regulations, feeding and release of wildlife in parks are already punishable with a fine of up to $5,000.

sections.label: New section 5A bans feeding birds
sections.summary: The new section 5A will make it illegal to feed all wild birds and introduces a higher penalty for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It affects their entire cycle." NParks further added that, "Short-term culling actually reduces competition, so the remaining birds have less competition to eat and mate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We often see an increase in the number of birds after periods of culling." The new section 5A will make it illegal to feed all wild birds and also introduces a higher penalty for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Higher penalties and forfeiture of conveyances
sections.summary: The Bill proposes significantly higher penalties for wildlife offences without approval, strengthened NParks enforcement powers, and court forfeiture of conveyances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As such, the Bill proposes to increase the penalties significantly for offences related to the killing, trapping, taking, keeping, offering for sale, sale, export and import of wildlife without approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As I have shared earlier, we are also strengthening NParks' enforcement powers and proposing a new power for the Court to be able to forfeit conveyances used in the commission of a convicted offence.

sections.label: Seizure and forfeiture of conveyances
sections.summary: Walter Theseira raised concerns about new sections 11B on seizure and 12C on forfeiture, especially for conveyances, noting similarity to existing seizure provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira raised some concerns about the new section 11B on seizure and section 12C on forfeiture, particularly as they relate to conveyances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This new provision on seizure is similar to other seizure provisions in existing legislation, such as section 51 of the Animals and Birds Act and section 35 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

sections.label: Court may not forfeit conveyances
sections.summary: Section 12C(1)(a) indicates the Court may not forfeit conveyances if the person is not convicted, such as when NParks compounds the offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Section 12C(1)(a) also indicates that the Court may not forfeit conveyances if the person is not convicted of the offence, for example, if NParks chose to compound the offence.

sections.label: Feeding stray cats and dogs
sections.summary: The current Wild Animals and Birds Act and the proposed amendments do not penalise feeding stray cats or dogs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The current Wild Animals and Birds Act and the proposed amendments do not penalise the feeding of stray cats or dogs.

sections.label: Feeding wildlife raises populations
sections.summary: The speaker agrees on helping the public appreciate wildlife but says research clearly shows feeding wildlife causes an unnatural rise in wildlife population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I agree that we should find ways to help the public appreciate wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But the research is very clear: the feeding of wildlife causes an unnatural rise in wildlife population.

sections.label: Bill bans wildlife feeding
sections.summary: A letter described nature lovers feeding birds and fish cooked rice, white bread or leftovers, and the Bill's proposed ban will reduce human-wildlife conflict and safeguard wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The letter continued, "I have seen many uninitiated 'nature lovers' feeding birds and fish with cooked rice, white bread or even leftover food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: These may not only make the wildlife ill but also wreak havoc on the eco-system." This Bill, and its proposed ban on wildlife feeding, will reduce human-wildlife conflict, address public safety concerns and safeguard the welfare of wildlife and our eco-system.

sections.label: Private property residents not excluded
sections.summary: It is not practical or reasonable to exclude residents of private properties from the ban on wildlife feeding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: For this reason, it is not practical or reasonable to exclude residents of private properties from the ban on wildlife feeding.

sections.label: Wildlife feeding penalties alignment
sections.summary: The Bill aligns the new Wildlife Act's penalty framework with the Parks and Trees Regulations and other animal-related Acts, with higher penalties applying to nature reserves and national parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: With regard to the feeding of wildlife, the higher penalties in the Parks and Trees Act apply to nature reserves and national parks, as those contain our most sensitive eco-systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to align the penalty framework in the new Wildlife Act with that in the Parks and Trees Regulations and other animal-related Acts, in order to rationalise the penalties across the various pieces of legislation.

sections.label: Subaraj and Act amendments
sections.summary: At a wake, a woman told the speaker that Subaraj and she had recently discussed the proposed amendments to the Wild Animals and Birds Act, which excited him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The first thing she told me at the wake was about how Subaraj and she were recently talking about the proposed amendments to the Wild Animals and Birds Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In fact, the last time I met Subaraj was at the final face-to-face public consultation for the Wild Animals and Birds Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: She told me how excited Subaraj was about the amendments.

sections.label: Thanking Members and Subaraj
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Members for supporting the Bill and, on behalf of Subaraj, thanks everyone for speaking up and fighting for wildlife and nature spots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: He continued being on the ground in our nature reserves, he continued passionately fighting and championing our cause and he continued to speak up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It's their time now, time to pass the baton." I thank Members for your support for this Bill and on behalf of Subaraj, I thank everyone for speaking up and for fighting for our wildlife and for our nature spots.

sections.label: WALRC consultations and Bill aims
sections.summary: The WALRC, with various representatives, held two years of public and closed-door consultations, and the Bill seeks to control wildlife feeding and release, require wildlife-related measures, introduce offences and penalties, and enhance enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The WALRC comprises of representatives from the nature community, animal welfare community, the Singapore Pest Management Association, the Pet Enterprise and Traders Association of Singapore, the Buddhist Federation, academic and legal community and the Nee Soon East Youth Network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We conducted extensive public consultations over the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We started with a face-to-face public consultation, followed by an online consultation on REACH where we received over 1,000 responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This was followed by another round of face-to-face public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We also held closed-door consultations with the pest management companies and separately with religious leaders and also obtained feedback from the MND Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, it seeks to: (a) control the feeding and release of wildlife in Singapore; (b) enable the Director-General, Wildlife Management of NParks to require wildlife-related measures to be implemented to address the impact of developments or works in relation to wildlife; (c) introduce new offences and enhance criminal penalties in the Act; and (d) enhance enforcement powers in the Act.
